x4_cells.goal: Validate the signed 12-to-24-bit hierarchical fold architecture at 752 MHz with exactly-once registered-SRAM consumption and full 16-bit k_dim support.
bugs_found: The accumulator architecture is no longer the critical path. A redundant issued<k_dim_q comparison was synthesized into a 15-stage control cone from issued[0] to both external request outputs, causing two setup violations.
x4_cells.learnings: The hierarchical fold moved the bottleneck from arithmetic to request control. Remove the redundant progress comparator from the S_REQ output decode before Y2. The next clean data path has about 30 ps slack at 752 MHz, implying about 774 MHz headroom under the same 20% I/O budget; choose 760 MHz for Y2 after the control repair.

x4_cells.goal: Remove Y1 request-control comparator cone and close strictly above 752 MHz at 760 MHz.
x4_cells.rtl_change: removed redundant issued<k_dim_q predicate from state-qualified paired request decode
bugs_found: Y2 launch wrapper copied x4_y1 artifact paths after completion; independent preservation and a final direct copy from the live x4_y2 ORFS tree recovered canonical Y2 evidence before cleanup.
x4_cells.learnings: Removing the request comparator closes 760 MHz. The new worst path is drain_col[0] to out_wdata[12] through an 18-cell combined row/column readout cone. Split readout selection across registered stages before raising the target.

x4_cells.goal: Split Y2 combined row/column readout selector and close strictly at 780 MHz.
x4_cells.rtl_change: registered selected accumulator row in S_DRAIN_LOAD before column selection in S_DRAIN_WRITE
x4_cells.learnings: The registered readout split raised extracted fmax from 783.569 to 837.683 MHz. The new worst path is chunk_accum[57][1] to wide_accum[57][16] through 21 cells in the signed 24-bit fold carry chain. Split the fold into registered low/high 12-bit slices before Y4.

x4_cells.goal: Split the Y3 24-bit fold carry chain into registered 12-bit slices and close at 820 MHz.
x4_cells.rtl_change: split signed 24-bit fold into registered low/high 12-bit additions with explicit carry
bugs_found: Two extracted max-capacitance violations remain despite clean timing, routing, DRC, antenna, slew, and fanout checks.
x4_cells.learnings: The registered fold split raised extracted fmax from 837.683 to 900.93 MHz and moved the worst setup path to the 12-bit per-cycle chunk accumulator. Y5 must preserve this architecture, strengthen report-driven capacitance repair beyond CAP_MARGIN=22, and select a target below the measured 900.93 MHz ceiling.

x4_cells.goal: Repair Y4's extracted max-capacitance failures with report-driven CAP_MARGIN=30 and close monotonically higher at 880 MHz.
x4_cells.physical_design_change: raised CAP_MARGIN from 22 to 30 based on Y4's two extracted max-capacitance violations
bugs_found: The first Y5 launch synced RTL to the wrong remote directory and failed before synthesis; the corrected launch produced the canonical physical result.
x4_cells.learnings: CAP_MARGIN=30 removed Y4's two extracted capacitance violations while preserving the registered fold architecture and closing 880 MHz. X4 finishes at 909.621 MHz extracted fmax; the remaining worst path is a 19-cell chunk-to-low-wide-accumulator path. X5 remains pending by protocol.
